reason: Both plans satisfy every hard requirement (phased structure with percentages/entry criteria, 5 correctly formatted RISK lines, decommissioning cleanly separated from the final migration batch, numeric halt threshold, and the required PHASES line), but Response B is slightly tighter: its phase-gate criteria explicitly reference a single, well-defined set of Go/No-Go metrics (including dollar- and multiplier-based guardrails) rather than introducing separate, untied accuracy thresholds as Response A does, and its sub-batch sizes are stated in absolute numbers rather than an ambiguous '~10%' base.
